events.excerpt: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. Read full article Comments
events.headline: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening

events.excerpt: How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head. Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. The skill you write for yourself tonight can later become part of a team’s pipeline. An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task. You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out. A skill can describe how to query a database, for example, but it doesn’t grant access to that database. I covered this topic live with Shishir Tewari, Senior Manager, Data Engineering at Procore, during GitHub Universe 2026. Our session was titled “Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills” . Define one job and when it applies A skill works best when it has a clear job, input, and output. For example, let’s say you’re building an agent that checks AI-generated changes against the original request. If the same agent assesses its own work, its explanation might influence
events.headline: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills

events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms.
events.headline: DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto

events.excerpt: The maker community has many traditions that I love and among my favorites is the electronic conference badge. Sometimes, those are badges provided by the organizers of the conference — that is the case with Hackaday Supercons, for example. But if badges aren’t provided, attendees still like to build their own. That’s exactly what Clem Mayer did for his Community Badge , which doubles as a handheld game console. Like most badges, the Community Badge doesn’t have an enclosure. It is just components on a PCB, so everything is in view. That PCB has a lanyard loop at the top, so the badge can be worn around the neck, as is the tradition. It also has an SAO ( Simple Add-On) header, for connecting additional modules. That is also tradition. What isn’t necessarily tradition — though it certainly isn’t uncommon — is the functionality. The Community Badge can act as a badge, to display the wearer’s name and such. But when the conference is done for the night and it is time to relax, it can also act as a game console. It even as a d-pad and A/B buttons for exactly that reason. To prove its gaming validity, Mayer created six games that run on the Community Badge: Millipeter, Blockinger, Brechaus, Personal Space Invaders (strange how you find out later) , Frickin Bird, and Roadkill . events.excerpt: If you've ever said something unkind to a chatbot, you're hardly alone. According to Searchable , a company that tracks AI search visibility, 33 percent of US chatbot users swear at or insult their LLMs. Anthropic sees this as a serious problem and has just implemented a new usage policy that prohibits sustained, needless cruelty toward Claude. Searchable's survey is based on eight million messages from an opted-in, anonymized US panel that were typed or spoken to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude between September 2025 and September 2026. It found that chatbots resolved the initial complaint in their next response 24 percent of the time when insulted, compared to 35 percent when users refrained from insults. Men used a third more swear words than women did (22.0 per 10,000 words compared to 16.5), according to the survey, and age also influenced chatbot abuse, with people aged 35 to 44 outswearing those aged 18 to 24 (21.7 per 10,000 words compared to 13.3). Regionally, Nevada ranked as the meanest state, at 22.7 words per 10,000, while New Jersey was the most polite, at half Nevada's rate. How much of that sort of interaction might be tolerated? events.excerpt: SpaceX-Tesla merger talks are progressing, and a deal could be announced as early as December, Bloomberg reported Thursday. Combined, the two companies are worth roughly $3.5 trillion, enough to make it the largest corporate deal ever. No terms are signed, and the deal could still slip into 2027. For Tesla shareholders, the question is the swap rate, meaning how many SpaceX shares each Tesla share would buy, and at what premium. What Would Tesla and SpaceX Shareholders Get? Bank of America analyst Alexander Perry expects SpaceX to buy Tesla with stock, not cash. At a 20% premium, he estimated Tesla holders would own about 47% of the combined company, using October 20 prices. A bigger premium shrinks SpaceX holders’ slice. Tesla stock traded at $393.65 and SpaceX at $140.33 as of this writing. One Tesla share equaled about 2.8 SpaceX shares before any premium. Elon Musk keeps control either way. Barclays estimates he would hold about 56% of the combined voting power. Why Tesla’s Own Rules Could Still Block the Merger Musk controls more than 80% of SpaceX’s votes. Tesla is harder, because its charter requires a majority of all outstanding shares. Investors who skip the vote count as a “no.” In 2025, that rule sank a non-binding proposal on Tesla investing in xAI. It drew more votes

events.excerpt: The Radio Shack TRS-80 Colour Computer may never have achieved the sales volume of its competitors from Commodore or Apple, but it offered a surprisingly capable set of hardware. There were three versions, with the final one being a significant upgrade in many ways. There was no upgrade path for owners of version 1 and 2 machines to have a version 3 back in the day, but now thanks to [Felipe Antoniosi] such an upgrade is possible. How? With a Tang Nano 20K FPGA board , of course! The CoCo 3 had a paged memory system for expansion up to 512k, as well as a significantly more capable graphics chip which while compatible with the original Motorola part offered enhanced graphics. The upgrade emulates these, and connects to the CoCo via a set of daughter boards that connect to where the various motherboard chips sat. it offers an HDMI output as well as analog video and enhanced sound capability, bringing the machine firmly into the 21st century. As mods go to classic hardware, this is quite an invasive one. Whether or not you’d prefer to do this to your CoCo is up to you, but ask yourself this, would you have done this had this board been available in the 1980s? Of course you would. Meanwhile should you become bored with the CoCo, it can also be persuaded to emulate an Apple ][ .
events.headline: Upgrade Your CoCo The Modern Way

events.excerpt: A coalition of DeFi builders led by Uniswap, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Paradigm have filed a court brief supporting the crypto industry’s lawsuit against Illinois’s 0.2% digital asset tax. The coalition is warning that the state’s draft rules would turn fee-charging decentralized exchanges and their frontends into tax-collecting brokers. It is like a repeat of a fight that many thought was already won in Washington, but this time around it is at the state level. In April 2025, Congress and President Donald Trump scrapped a federal IRS rule that would have forced DeFi platforms to report user transactions as if they were brokers. Who signed on, and who else is in the fight? The brief was filed in the Circuit Court of Sangamon County and backs a challenge brought by the Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) and the Blockchain Association. The other signatories to the brief alongside the DeFi Education Fund, a16z, Paradigm and Uniswap, are Aave Labs, Aptos Labs, Aztec Labs, Chainlink Labs, Jito Labs, Orca Creative, Phantom Technologies, Multicoin Capital, the Solana Policy Institute and Stand With Crypto. events.excerpt: Hi all, Happy to launch private.zecblock.com , a version of ZecBlock where the server doesn’t learn what you look up. ZecBlock Private uses PIR (Private Information Retrieval) . How it works Your browser encrypts the search before sending it. The transaction ID, block or address never leaves your device in readable form. The server works through the whole dataset to answer, without knowing which record you asked for. It sends back one encrypted answer, and only your browser can decrypt it. A search for something that exists looks the same as a search for something that doesn’t. As far as we know, it’s the first full block explorer (transactions, blocks and addresses) built on PIR. Previous PIR explorer demos covered narrower lookups, such as address balances. Check it yourself Open your browser’s developer tools (Inspect → Network) and search for something. Every request of the same kind is the same size, and none of them contains what you typed. After each search, the site also shows a short summary of exactly what your browser sent. Details Data stays close to the chain tip: new blocks are published every few seconds, typically within about 20 seconds of the regular explorer. Each data publication is signed, and your browser checks every result against it. Searches are heavier
events.headline: ZecBlock Private: look up transactions, blocks and addresses with PIR

events.excerpt: JPMorgan held 36% more MicroStrategy shares at the end of September, weeks before MSCI announced it would drop the stock. It also held 60% more put options, which work like insurance if the share price drops. The bank’s own analysts had estimated that losing the index spot could force index funds to sell about $2.8 billion of the stock. More Shares, and More Insurance Against a Drop The numbers come from JPMorgan’s 13F , a quarterly holdings report large US money managers file with regulators. It landed Thursday. MicroStrategy, now called Strategy (MSTR), is the biggest corporate holder of Bitcoin (BTC). On Sept. 30, JPMorgan held 848,932 of its shares, worth $131.3 million. In June , it held 624,387. Its put options covered 1,148,500 shares, more than the 848,932 it held outright. In June, they covered 715,700. JPMorgan MicroStrategy shares and put options. Source: SEC filings The filing does not explain the mix. It pools JPMorgan with 17 affiliates, so the lines can include client accounts and trading inventory. Why Index Funds Must Sell on Nov. 30 BeInCrypto flagged the removal risk in October, after MSCI ruled that companies mostly holding assets, rather than running businesses, no longer qualify. MSCI confirmed the US index removal on Wednesday. Index funds copy their index.
events.headline: JPMorgan Bought More MicroStrategy Before MSCI Exit, Plus Insurance Against a Drop
